question: What primary substance do whole fruits provide that slows digestion and supports gastrointestinal transit?
explanation: Plant cell walls contain abundant dietary fiber, which adds bulk to stool and delays gastric emptying. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h1)

question: How do the antioxidants found naturally in fresh fruits primarily protect human cells?
explanation: Antioxidants donate electrons to unstable free radicals, stabilizing them and preventing oxidative stress on cells. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h1)

question: What is the general recommended daily fruit intake range for healthy adult humans?

options.B: Less than half a cup daily

explanation: Standard dietary guidelines advise adults to consume between 1.5 and 2 cups of fruit each day to meet micronutrient needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h2)

question: Why do toddlers require smaller absolute serving sizes of fruit compared to active adolescents?

options.A: They possess lower total daily energy expenditures
options.B: Their stomachs cannot absorb water-soluble vitamins
options.C: Their diets must consist exclusively of fats
options.D: They completely lack enzymes to process fructose

explanation: Smaller body size and lower basal metabolic needs mean younger children require fewer total calories and smaller portion volumes. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h2)

question: Why does drinking fruit juice cause a faster blood sugar spike than eating the equivalent whole fruit?

options.A: Commercial juices contain added animal proteins that accelerate digestion
options.B: Liquid foods bypass the stomach entirely and enter the bloodstream directly
options.C: Processed juices have higher molecular weights than whole fruit pulp
options.D: The extraction process removes dietary fiber that slows sugar absorption

explanation: Without fiber to trap sugars and slow gastric emptying, liquid fructose and glucose enter the small intestine rapidly. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of whole fruit consumption?
explanation: Whole fruits are rich in dietary fiber, whereas extracted and strained juices have very little. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h3)

question: What visual everyday object approximates a medium-sized whole fruit like an apple or orange?
explanation: A medium piece of whole fruit is traditionally compared in size to a tennis ball or a fist. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h4)

question: A patient asks why their recommended portion size for dried mangoes is much smaller than fresh mango slices. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Dried fruit must be chewed longer, which damages tooth enamel if eaten in large cups
options.B: The dehydration process destroys all vitamins, requiring strict limits to prevent toxicity
options.C: Drying removes water and concentrates natural sugars, making smaller amounts equal in calories
options.D: Dried fruits are coated in synthetic chemicals that expand inside the stomach

explanation: Removing water concentrates the macronutrients, meaning a smaller physical volume packs significantly more sugar and calories. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h4)

question: Why is it clinically advantageous for Nigerian nurses to recommend local seasonal fruits over imported varieties?

options.A: Local options are more affordable and accessible for average households
options.B: Seasonal Nigerian fruits do not require any chewing or digestion
options.C: Imported fruits are chemically altered to contain zero vitamins
options.D: Local tropical fruits contain no natural sugars whatsoever

explanation: Dietary advice is only effective when patients can realistically afford and source the recommended foods within their local economy. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h5)

question: Which of the following fruits is widely grown, accessible, and seasonal in West Africa?
explanation: Pawpaw (papaya) thrives in tropical West African climates, making it a locally abundant and affordable fruit source. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h5)

question: What is a primary logistical barrier to fresh fruit consumption in many developing tropical regions?

options.A: Mandatory government taxes on all raw agricultural goods
options.B: Universal laws banning the domestic transport of citrus
options.C: Inadequate cold-chain storage and high post-harvest loss
options.D: An absolute lack of arable soil for any plant life

explanation: Without reliable refrigeration and rapid transport, perishable fruits spoil quickly before reaching consumers in markets. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h6)

question: Which nursing strategy helps a busy patient incorporate more fresh fruit into their daily routine?

options.A: Suggesting portable whole fruits that require minimal preparation
options.B: Telling them to cook all fruits until they lose their structure
options.C: Instructing them to replace all water intake with fresh lime juice
options.D: Recommending they buy only expensive imported canned varieties

explanation: Portable options like bananas or apples make adherence easier for individuals with hectic, time-constrained schedules. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h6)
